scenarios.label: Two accepts race
scenarios.summary: Two dispatch offers reach the same driver before either caller sees the other result.
trace: Trip A and Trip B both read the driver as available.
The driver accepts both offers from separate retries.
The trip service must choose one durable owner.
The losing command receives the committed assignment instead of creating another one.

responses.label: Atomic claim with a version check
responses.detail: Condition the write on driver availability and the expected version, then emit the assignment through an outbox.
responses.customerImpact: One rider gets the driver; the other request resumes candidate search.
responses.operatorAction: Track claim conflicts and match retries by city and cell.

responses.label: Process-local mutex
responses.detail: Serialize accepts inside one matcher process without a durable ownership check.
responses.customerImpact: Both riders can see the same driver until reconciliation cancels one trip.
responses.operatorAction: Reconcile active-trip ownership and replace local coordination with a durable conditional write.

responses.label: Last write wins
responses.detail: Accept both commands and keep whichever assignment arrives last.
responses.customerImpact: A confirmed rider can silently lose the driver.
responses.operatorAction: Repair rider and driver state, then audit every downstream notification.

scenarios.label: Location stream stalls
scenarios.summary: A driver remains in the geo index after the app disconnects and stops sending fresh coordinates.
trace: The last location update is accepted with a driver sequence number.
The app disconnects, but the geo point remains queryable.
Matching reads the candidate and checks its update age.
Expired availability is removed or ignored before an offer is sent.

responses.label: Sequence number plus freshness lease
responses.detail: Ignore out-of-order updates and require an unexpired availability lease before offering the trip.
responses.customerImpact: The rider may wait longer, but does not receive a driver known to be stale.
responses.operatorAction: Measure stale-candidate rejection rate and location age percentiles.

responses.label: Trust arrival order
responses.detail: Treat the last packet received by the server as the newest location and keep it indefinitely.
responses.customerImpact: The rider waits for a driver who may be offline or far away.
responses.operatorAction: Expire the stale point and investigate sequence gaps by connection.

responses.label: Confirm through a global database
responses.detail: Synchronously read a global source of truth before scoring every nearby driver.
responses.customerImpact: Matching latency grows with cross-region reads and dependency load.
responses.operatorAction: Move bounded freshness into the regional hot path.

scenarios.label: Payment capture times out
scenarios.summary: The trip completes, the payment provider times out, and the client retries without knowing whether capture succeeded.
trace: The trip service commits completed distance, duration, and fare inputs.
A payment command is published with a stable trip-scoped key.
The provider response times out after an uncertain result.
A retry reuses the key and reconciliation records the final ledger state.

responses.label: Stable idempotency key and reconciliation
responses.detail: Retry the same capture identity, persist provider references, and reconcile uncertain outcomes asynchronously.
responses.customerImpact: The receipt can show payment pending without blocking trip completion.
responses.operatorAction: Reconcile pending captures and alert on age, not a single timeout.

responses.label: Create a new charge on every retry
responses.detail: Treat each timeout as a fresh payment attempt with a new provider identity.
responses.customerImpact: The rider can be charged more than once for one trip.
responses.operatorAction: Stop retries, refund duplicates, and reconcile by trip ID.

responses.label: Roll back trip completion
responses.detail: Return the trip to in-progress until the payment provider responds.
responses.customerImpact: Driver and rider apps disagree about whether the ride ended.
responses.operatorAction: Restore completed state and separate trip truth from payment settlement.

scenarios.label: Safety report during outage
scenarios.summary: A rider sends an emergency report while ordinary notifications and payment services are degraded.
trace: The client sends the report with trip ID, actor ID, location, and timestamp.
The edge authenticates and durably acknowledges the safety event.
A dedicated workflow pages the response team and preserves an audit trail.
Ordinary trip, notification, and payment recovery continue independently.

responses.label: Dedicated durable safety workflow
responses.detail: Give safety reports separate admission control, durable storage, escalation, access policy, and operational ownership.
responses.customerImpact: The report is acknowledged and routed even while noncritical services are degraded.
responses.operatorAction: Verify acknowledgement latency, responder pickup time, and audit-log completeness.

responses.label: Use the ordinary notification queue
responses.detail: Publish the report at the same priority and through the same capacity pool as receipts and promotions.
responses.customerImpact: The rider sees an acknowledgement without a bounded responder handoff.
responses.operatorAction: Move safety work to isolated capacity and replay the delayed event.

responses.label: Wait for payment recovery first
responses.detail: Block the safety workflow until payment and trip services are fully healthy.
responses.customerImpact: A financial dependency delays urgent human response.
responses.operatorAction: Bypass nonessential dependencies and page the safety owner immediately.
